handbookNote: Source: official 'Driver's Licensing Handbook, State of West Virginia' (Revised 07/2022), published by the WV Department of Transportation, Division of Motor Vehicles, retrieved directly from the DMV's own site. transportation.wv.gov/DMV now 301-redirects to dmv.wv.gov; the handbook was located via dmv.wv.gov -> 'Driver's Licensing Handbooks' page, which links the PDF at https://webapps.transportation.wv.gov/TWS/WVDOTDocumentStorageMigration/PDF/Transportation/DMV/DMVFormSearch/Drivers_Licensing_Handbook_web.pdf. Downloaded directly via curl (7.9MB PDF) and extracted natively with pdftotext -layout (not OCR) to temp/handbooks/wv/driver.txt (also saved as driver_full.txt), yielding about 4,280 lines / 289KB of text across Chapters I-IX plus a definitions section. Note: this particular PDF's font has a broken ToUnicode CMap for 'fi'/'fl' ligatures, so extracted text shows artifacts like 'trafc' for traffic, 'ofce' for office, and 'infuence' for influence -- a cosmetic extraction quirk, not a content gap; all facts below were read past this artifact directly from the source PDF text, and no question text quotes the glitched spelling. Exam mechanics were found directly in the handbook itself (not guessed, not borrowed from another state): Chapter IV, 'Knowledge Examination' section (p.24) states verbatim that 'The knowledge examination has at least 25 questions' and 'You must answer 19 out of the 25 questions correctly to pass the test. There is a time limit on the test and any questions not answered in the prescribed time will be considered incorrect.' That gives 25 items, a 76% (19/25) passing score, and a stated (but unspecified-duration) time limit -- confirmed from the primary source, no secondary corroboration needed since the number is explicit in the official handbook text. Content depth: this handbook is substantial and well-organized -- Ch. I Driver's License Information (REAL ID, first-time/renewal documentation, the full 3-level GDL program with ages/hours/passenger and curfew restrictions/conviction penalties, motorcycle permits and endorsements, license restriction codes, 'Drive for Five' renewal cycle); Ch. II Driver Responsibilities (point system and point-value table, compulsory insurance minimums, hands-free cell phone law with fine schedule, mandatory revocation list); Ch. III DUI (BAC thresholds for over/under 21, implied consent, Interlock Program, drowsy driving); Ch. IV Examination Procedures (vision screening, illegal equipment list, automatic-failure lists for both the basic control skills and road tests); Ch. V Traffic Control Devices (sign shapes/colors, traffic signals, lane-use signals, pavement markings, railroad crossings); Ch. VI Traffic Laws (speed limits by road type, following distance, turning/parking/passing rules, detailed prohibited-parking distance table, right-of-way, and a full 'sharing the road' set covering pedestrians, school buses, motorcycles, heavy trucks/No-Zone, animal riders, bicycles); Ch. VII Interstate Driving; Ch. VIII Defensive Driving (weather hazards including hydroplaning thresholds and stopping-distance-on-ice multipliers, safety belts/child seats/ABS/airbags); and Ch. IX Emergency Situations and First Aid. This comfortably supported 278 distinct, grounded, non-repetitive multiple-choice questions across 13 topic buckets, every one traceable to a specific chapter/section/page of this handbook -- no invented facts, no numbers borrowed from any other state's handbook or from general 'common driving knowledge' not actually present in this source. One deliberate omission for honesty: the DUI penalty chart on p.22 (fines/jail time by offense tier) suffered column-misalignment from the PDF's table layout during extraction, so only the two clearly-stated zero-tolerance revocation periods (30 days first offense, 60 days or until age 18 second offense) were used from that chart -- the more granular 2nd/3rd-DUI fine and jail-time figures were deliberately excluded rather than risk mispairing garbled numbers to the wrong offense tier.
